title: The Limits of Static Training Knowledge
text: Hi, I am Deepa Shenoy. In this video is about how RAG gives AI access to external knowledge. This is Liam narrating for Deepa. A language model draws on patterns learned during training and on the context it receives. It may not know a specific, current, or private fact you need. Imagine asking an assistant, "What is our company's remote work policy?" That policy is private and it may have changed. Before answering,

title: The Query Example: Retrieving Private Remote Work Policies
text: The system searches an approved company knowledge base and retrieves a relevant policy passage. It adds that passage to the question as context. Now, the model has specific information to work from. In our fictional example, if the policy says remote work is allowed 2 days a week, the assistant can explain that rule. That is retrieval augmented generation. Retrieve first, add context, then generate. External sources can include

title: The RAG Cycle: Retrieve First, Add Context, Then Generate
text: Documents, databases, or other approved knowledge sources. The model is not retrained for each question. This connects to my last video on AI hallucinations. Relevant retrieved context can help reduce unsupported claims, but RAG does not guarantee correctness. Retrieval and source quality still matter. Check the answer against its source.
